title: Rejecting a stale write
questions: Explain expected version 7 vs stored version 8, then the matching version 7 vs 7. Show the stored value stays unchanged on rejection. The comparison and write are one database statement, not two operations.

slide.title: One conditional UPDATE rejects stale writes
slide.narrative: The database checks the ID and expected version in the same statement that changes the document. A rejected update leaves the stored body and version unchanged. A missing ID also returns 409. The function does not retry automatically.

fileSummaries.summary: Replaces an unconditional overwrite with one atomic update that requires a matching ID and version.

svgIllustration.title: A version match controls the whole update
svgIllustration.takeaway: A mismatch changes nothing. A match replaces the body and increases the version in one database statement.
svgIllustration.assumptions: Both examples use the existing ID D1 and supplied body New. Values are illustrative, not production measurements. Each example starts independently.

plan.question: What changes when expected version 7 meets stored version 8 or stored version 7?
plan.visualApproach: Show two independent before-and-after examples with the stored body and version inside one atomic UPDATE boundary.
plan.whyThisForm: Stable positions make an unchanged row visible on rejection and show both stored fields changing together on success.
plan.encodings: The outer boundary contains the condition and mutation in one statement. The inner row keeps the stored body and version together. Text states each result; color only reinforces it.
plan.motion: Keep the input, UPDATE boundary, and stored row fixed. At the statement result, leave both stored values unchanged for rejection or change both together for success. Reveal the affected-row count and response in that same result frame.
plan.prediction: With expected version 7, another stored version cannot match, so the statement leaves the row unchanged and the function returns 409.
plan.restingState: Each result retains the supplied version, statement condition, stored body and version, affected-row count, and response.

scenarios.title: Expected 7, stored 8: reject
scenarios.input: Existing ID D1; expected version 7; supplied body New; stored body Old and version 8.

frames.title: The supplied version is stale
frames.caption: The condition and both possible field changes belong to one atomic UPDATE.

frames.title: Rejection preserves both stored values
frames.caption: Version 8 does not match expected version 7. No row changes; the function returns 409.
